humanAcceptance.evidence: Dave instructed Codex to improve, mechanically test and publish the final exact Pass 72 candidate autonomously while preserving the retained releases. This is standing publication-first authorization, not preview acceptance: Dave did not inspect or test the immutable preview and will perform owner HITL only after the GitHub Pages build is live.

requirements.summary: Bind publication to Dave's standing publication-first authorization
requirements.expected: The exact immutable Pass 72 preview may enter the protected production workflow only after every required mechanical gate is green; this records authorization to publish, not preview inspection or completed gameplay HITL.
requirements.falsifier: Publication uses a different runtime SHA, bypasses a required mechanical gate, or represents Dave as having inspected or tested the immutable preview.

evidence.note: Dave's instruction provides standing publication-first authority for the mechanically green exact candidate. It does not provide preview inspection or public gameplay HITL evidence.

requirements.summary: Preserve the exact retained release topology while promoting Pass 72
requirements.expected: Pass 72 is the candidate and eventual live route; Pass 70 remains the exact previous release, Pass 69 remains byte-pinned, Pass 67.1 remains the non-selectable stable-source pin, and Pass 63 remains the selectable WebGL rollback across root, legacy and room routes. Rebuilt Pass 67.1 and Pass 63 bytes display the immutable publication timestamp of their pinned original Pages commit rather than the new Pass 72 build time.
requirements.falsifier: A retained channel disappears or changes identity, Pass 67.1 becomes selectable, a rebuilt fallback displays a timestamp other than its pinned original Pages publication, or a chooser, legacy or room route resolves to the wrong channel.

evidence.note: The topology and production-pipeline contracts pin the Pass 72, Pass 70, Pass 69, Pass 67.1 and Pass 63 identities, route policy and original Pages timestamps for retained-source rebuilds.
The served chooser test exercises all selectable choices plus root, legacy and room routing.

requirements.summary: Default private matches to FFA while retaining explicit TDM selection
requirements.expected: A new private lobby visibly defaults to free-for-all, the host can explicitly select team deathmatch, and FFA hostility remains player-based even when presentation team values match.
requirements.falsifier: A new lobby defaults to TDM, TDM cannot be selected, or matching presentation values make distinct FFA players friendly.

evidence.note: The lobby model contract covers FFA defaulting, explicit TDM selection and FFA hostility.

requirements.summary: Reset a hosted lobby to one distinct fresh room code
requirements.expected: Only the active host can reset; the old durable hosted-room key is synchronously cleared in the reset click turn before reload, and exactly one distinct replacement room code is opened and stored after Peer admission.
requirements.falsifier: A guest can reset, the invalidated room remains recoverable in storage, a duplicate host attempt is opened, or the replacement code is blank or equal to the old code.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/host-room-recovery.test.ts src/network-connection-attempt.test.ts src/pass72-lobby-reset-contract.test.ts --reporter=dot
evidence.note: The production storage helper, exactly-once connection attempt model and integration contract cover host authority, synchronous invalidation and fresh-code recovery.
The native browser test reads localStorage in the reset click turn, then verifies a nonempty distinct room code and its durable replacement value.

requirements.summary: Replicate safe squad names and colours without changing combat teams
requirements.expected: Bounded squad names and six-digit colours replicate from guest to host, render as injection-safe roster text and a visible colour swatch, and remain presentation metadata with no effect on hostility.
requirements.falsifier: Invalid metadata is admitted, replicated values do not reach both rosters, the colour is not visibly rendered, injection markup executes, or squad metadata changes combat hostility.

evidence.note: The production squad parser and roster renderer are tested for bounds, legacy compatibility, safe rendering and hostility separation.
The host-and-guest browser test changes the guest squad name and colour and checks replicated DOM text plus computed swatch colour.

requirements.summary: Apply the exact M14 EBR damage envelope
requirements.expected: The M14 EBR uses a 37.2 base and 24 minimum body-damage envelope, 38-to-100 metre falloff and a 1.7 head multiplier in both gameplay and the canonical weapon catalog.
requirements.falsifier: Either runtime or catalog differs from any authored value, or close, head or maximum-range computed damage escapes the pinned contract.

evidence.note: The gameplay computation and canonical catalog independently pin the M14 base, minimum, falloff and head multiplier.

requirements.summary: Halve fall damage without moving its impact thresholds
requirements.expected: Authoritative fall damage remains zero through the 9.5 metre-per-second safe threshold, scales through the existing envelope, reaches 50 at 22 metres per second and never exceeds 50.
requirements.falsifier: Either threshold moves, an ordinary landing gains damage, maximum fall damage differs from 50, or invalid inputs produce damage.

evidence.note: The authoritative fall-damage contract pins 9.5 and 22 metre-per-second thresholds, the halved 50-point cap and fail-closed invalid input.

requirements.summary: Use the 0.24 metre flare projectile radius without weakening authority
requirements.expected: The flare projectile resolves with a bounded 0.24 metre radius while retaining occlusion, direct-hit, burn, duplicate-action, prediction and authority-migration protections.
requirements.falsifier: The radius differs from 0.24 metres, a flare admits a through-wall target, a peer prediction causes damage, or replay and migration can duplicate a hit or burn pulse.

evidence.note: The flare system tests the widened bounded intersection together with occlusion, authoritative lifecycle, replay and prediction constraints.

requirements.summary: Attribute Carpet Bomber deaths to the map without recursive streak credit
requirements.expected: Carpet Bomber impact and residual-fire deaths resolve as environment kills under the canonical map killer identity, retain the victim's authoritative damage/death totals, broadcast the updated scoreboard and emit a canonical Carpet Bomber feed/diagnostic entry without a synthetic map score, player kill or recursive streak credit.
requirements.falsifier: A Carpet Bomber victim death is missing from authoritative scores, the score update is not broadcast, feed or diagnostics identify an unknown/player killer, a map PlayerScore appears, the activating player receives the kill, hosted occlusion is bypassed, or a replay duplicates residual damage.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/kill-provenance.test.ts src/authoritative-death-outcome.test.ts src/carpet-death-main-integration.test.ts src/carpet-ground-fire-multiplayer.test.ts --reporter=dot
evidence.note: Behavioral death-outcome and real processDeath integration tests pin victim-only death scoring, score broadcast wiring, canonical environment feed/diagnostics, no synthetic map row or player kill, while the hosted residual-fire suite covers occlusion, receipts and replay deduplication.

requirements.summary: Break glass from hosted explosive-crossbow detonations through the shared occlusion policy
requirements.expected: An admitted explosive-crossbow detonation reaches the same host-owned, occlusion-aware and replicated glass mutation path as grenades, opening a pane only after the admitted impact is replicated.
requirements.falsifier: A guest mutates glass authoritatively, cover behind or before the pane is classified incorrectly, an explosion breaks through real cover, or peers receive an aperture before its admitted impact identity.

evidence.note: The integration seam, admission geometry and runtime replication tests cover shared crossbow/grenade policy, occlusion and impact-before-aperture ordering.

requirements.summary: Present support-shot audio to the correct audience while keeping feedback owner-only
requirements.expected: Every host-admitted Chopper or Drone shot plays once for its owner and for an eligible TDM teammate; enemies and same-team-valued FFA rivals hear neither, while damage HUD and tracers remain restricted to the support owner.
requirements.falsifier: A teammate misses admitted support audio, an enemy or FFA rival hears it, a non-owner receives damage feedback, a missed shot emits no shot event, or replay causes duplicate audio.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/support-combat-presentation.test.ts src/chopper-gunner-fire-ray.test.ts src/killstreak-runtime.test.ts src/killstreak-protocol.test.ts --reporter=dot
evidence.note: Behavioral tests cover owner and teammate playback, enemy and FFA exclusion, exact call counts, owner-only feedback, miss and cadence emission, replay bounds and strict transport validation.

requirements.summary: Keep death transitions host-authored on the protocol-18 topology
requirements.expected: Protocol 18 rejects cached protocol-17 peers before new wire fields can be discarded, initial guest joins using the reserved map: or host-bot- participant namespaces are rejected before credential binding, guest event connections drop forged death messages before app delivery, and validated host-authored death transitions still replicate to clients.
requirements.falsifier: A protocol-17 peer binds to the protocol-18 room, an initial guest join using map: or host-bot- binds a credential, a guest-authored death reaches the host application, or a host-authored death fails to reach the client event lane.

evidence.note: The participant-identity contract reserves exactly the map: and host-bot- namespaces while retaining ordinary participant IDs.

Protocol and real connection-lifecycle tests reject stale peers and reserved-namespace joins before credential binding, drop a forged guest death before host app delivery, preserve the next valid guest event and deliver the same validated death shape from host to client.

requirements.summary: Complete owner visual, audio, feel and network HITL on the public Pages build
requirements.expected: After protected publication, Dave can test the exact public Pass 72 Pages build for visual quality, support audio, weapon and movement feel, native browser behavior and real LAN, WAN and NAT multiplayer while retained channels remain available.
requirements.falsifier: The public build does not bind the released SHA, a retained fallback is inaccessible during review, or Dave reports a release-blocking defect in public HITL.

deferApproval.reason: Dave authorized publication first and reserved owner HITL for the public GitHub Pages build. He did not inspect or test the immutable preview; subjective visual, audio and feel review plus native browser and real LAN, WAN and NAT validation remain unperformed and explicitly deferred.
